main_text.p: ti, iamdudum ante ipse, eruditissime Leo, inculcasti ex Græcorum, & Latinorum consensu, quod plurimum Reformatorum latera vrget, & pectora ferit. Videns dein

quisque pro bono Ecclesiæ longiori vita dignus erat, idem hoc argumentum maiores sumere vires ex aliorum Orientalium consensione, duo nostro Hebediesu, dum illum vna cum nostris notis recudi curauit Moguntiæ, adiecit programmata ad Academicos Protestantes, quibus eos prouocat ad singulare hoc certamen. Præsertim cum non defuerint apud ipsos, qui meris, & nudis assertionibus Orientalium hunc consensum sibi vindicare sint conati, vti testis vberrimus, & omni exceptione maior, nobis esse potest vir clarissimus Iulius Blumius, qui vna nobiscum plures huius generis assertiones contulit Parisijs. Huius autem argumenti ex consensione tot populorum adstructum, vim, & efficaciam effugere, atq; euitare volentes Veielius, & Hottingerus, opposita prorsus diuerticula, & flexiones arripiunt, eodem tamen collimantes, neminem veritatem ipsam eludere. Veielius enim, vt se hinc citius expediat, hunc irridet, & improbat consensum, ita pag. 2. scribens:

page.notes: The Arabic line between "Videns dein" and "quisque" is marked [?] because the letters are not fully legible at this scan resolution. The line may be a set-off author name with an Arabic phrase, and the Arabic is uncertain. "opposita" has a Cyrillic-looking "a" in the printed text; it is a Latin word, so the letters should be Latin, and it is written here as printed with the doubtful letter flagged for review. The left edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
